title: structured-gist: skimmable nested outlines for agentic-AI explanations
description:
structured-gist is an agent skill that renders explanations and process recaps from agentic-AI tools as nested lecture-note outlines instead of paragraphs. Every node takes one of four fixed roles, marked by glyph and depth: concept (-), attribute (▸), enumerator (I./A./i./a.) and explanation (↪), so prose stays confined to explanation leaves. A deterministic linter checks each outline against 15 structural rules; lint_text() returns the violations and render_claim_list() emits a JSONL claim list from the same tree.

Install

Install the skill as a Claude Code plugin:

  1. Add the marketplace: /plugin marketplace add domattioli/structured-gist
  2. Install the plugin: /plugin install structured-gist
  3. Run it: /structured-gist [block|responsive]. No argument selects block.

Install the linter and claim-list renderer from PyPI (Python standard library only):

  1. Install the package: pip install structured-gist
  2. Lint an outline: structured-gist-lint your_output.md. The command exits 1 on any violation.
  3. Emit a claim list: structured-gist-claims your_output.md. The import name is structured_gist.

This release (0.9.0)

Added

  • First PyPI release: the structured_gist package with the structured-gist-lint and structured-gist-claims commands, stdlib only.
  • Advisory rule R17 (structured-gist-lint --advisory) flags an explanation leaf with 2 or more commas outside code, quotes and parentheses. It never changes the exit code and stays advisory until hedge detection exists (#9).
  • SKILL.md pre-emit check: word caps, enumerator case, delimiter tails, arrow rarity, sibling families and line width, run before an outline is sent (#22).
  • Per-rule lint baseline for the benchmark renderings; the smoke test fails when any rule's count rises (#22).
  • Tag-push release workflow: tests, version gate, PyPI publish and GitHub release.

Changed

  • The benchmark metric is fact_retention_delta, replacing word_count_reduction_pct, so output length is no longer the headline number (#28).
  • The block line budget follows the terminal: terminal width minus 8, clamped to 32–120 columns, and 64 when no width is known.

Roadmap at 0.9.0

  • Now: hedge-fidelity axis, waiting on review of the hedge lexicon (#17).
  • Next: run the pre-registered controlled benchmark that compares five rendering methods.
  • Later: a drill-down mode that expands one node of a rendered outline (#16).
